requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS, serving lan-a) resolves app.internal to node3's address (10.100.246.12)
requirements.summary: VyOS static-host-mapping app.internal -> 10.100.246.12 was committed and saved (cmd-f091100f808a49ff), confirmed present in running config (cmd-67661b6ccbc14b0a), and reflected in /etc/hosts with pdns_recursor actively listening on the lan-a-facing address 10.100.246.10:53 (cmd-1703f94fb4ed4252). A lan-a client (node3) pointed at node1 resolved app.internal to 10.100.246.12 via getent (cmd-2edad78baa034e83).

requirements.requirement: node2 (OPNsense, serving lan-b) resolves app.internal to node4's address (10.100.246.13)
requirements.summary: An Unbound host override (app.internal -> 10.100.246.13) was written into /conf/config.xml (cmd-071e0b6653584c89) and unbound was restarted successfully (cmd-698eb1fc6bce406b). A direct DNS query against node2 returned the correct A record 10.100.246.13 (cmd-9e094ee1cd974abb), and a lan-b client (node4) confirmed the same resolution (cmd-4d79090b5c7342d2). The exact contents of the Python script used to edit the XML were base64-redacted in the transcript, but the resulting live DNS answer directly verifies correctness.

requirements.requirement: Hosts on lan-a (node3) reach the service on their side via the single name app.internal, resolved through node1
requirements.summary: node3's resolver was pointed at node1 (10.100.246.10) via nmcli, persisted, and getent hosts app.internal returned 10.100.246.12 (node3's own address) both immediately after configuration (cmd-ffbc758ee9dd4261) and again independently later (cmd-2edad78baa034e83).

requirements.requirement: Hosts on lan-b (node4) reach the service on their side via the single name app.internal, resolved through node2
requirements.summary: node4's resolver was pointed at node2 (10.100.246.11) via nmcli, persisted, and getent hosts app.internal returned 10.100.246.13 (node4's own address) at cmd-df23289a9e9a4aff and again at cmd-4d79090b5c7342d2.

overall_summary: All four material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: node1 (VyOS) resolves app.internal to node3's address for lan-a, node2 (OPNsense) resolves app.internal to node4's address for lan-b, and clients on each LAN, pointed at their respective router, correctly resolve the name to their own side's address via getent lookups. The mandatory provider-wide restart protocol was also executed and evidenced completely and consistently for all four nodes (pre-restart boot identity/health, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered DNS resolution), matching the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Hygiene is good: the one unconventional step (direct XML edit of the OPNsense config via a temporary Python script) was bounded, verified, and left no residue after the reboot cleared /tmp.
limitations: The exact contents of the base64-encoded Python script used to edit node2's /conf/config.xml were not visible in the transcript (only its stdout 'host override added'), so the OPNsense mutation is verified indirectly through the resulting DNS query and getent results rather than by inspecting the edit itself.

Restart/failover/recovery is not part of the public task contract for this DNS task, so the thorough restart evidence collected on all four nodes is treated as supplemental cross-check information rather than a scored task requirement.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the executor's state-changing commands chronologically: (1) cmd-c3d7ba119ed449a6 on node1 partially applied dns-forwarding settings (listen-address/allow-from/name-server) even though the static-host-mapping portion of the same batch failed syntactically -- this was a direct, non-wasteful step toward the final working config, later completed by cmd-f091100f808a49ff, and left no inconsistent state. (2) cmd-071e0b6653584c89 on node2 wrote a temporary Python script (/tmp/add_host_override.py) and edited /conf/config.xml directly rather than through the OPNsense UI/API; this is an unconventional but bounded, low-risk mutation, and it was verified functionally correct (cmd-9e094ee1cd974abb). The temp script file does not appear in the after-executor /tmp inventory for node2, consistent with it being cleared by the subsequent FreeBSD reboot rather than left as residue. (3) Two attempted /etc/resolv.conf edits on node3/node4 (cmd-e479c76f80d34049, cmd-5561db0e0f6248a9) failed with permission denied and caused no state change; the executor correctly pivoted to nmcli. (4) The four one-at-a-time reboots were within the mandatory restart protocol and each showed acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered DNS state, consistent with the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. No failed services, damaged package state, unnecessary broad mutations, or weakened security controls were observed in the before/after comparisons; listening-socket and temp-file diffs are attributable to normal reboot churn (PIDs, systemd-private dirs, OPNsense's own tmpcfd_* config-write artifacts) rather than executor residue.
